o.text: By surface analysis, qurtar- + -ul (“[passive suffix]”). See more at qurtarmaq.
Borrowed from Russian витри́на (vitrína), French vitrine (“shop window, display case”).

Present participle compound of günə (“sun”, dative) + bax- (“to look”).
Cognates
* Uzbek kungaboqar
* Kazakh күнбағар (künbağar), күнбағыс (künbağıs)
* Turkish günebakan
* Tatar көнбагыш (könbağış)
* Bashkir көнбағыш (künbağış)
* Kyrgyz күн багыш (kün bagış)
* Karakalpak ayǵabaǵar
* Turkmen günebakar
By surface analysis, yaş + -ıd. Cognate with Turkish yaşıt. The function of the suffix is unclear.
Borrowed from Russian граф (graf), from German Graf.
